A dissent by RE Eggert argued the complaint was judicially out of order because the SJC lacks constitutional authority to review a presbytery's session-records review decisions under BCO 40-2 and 40-3.

artifacts.synopsis: RE Tom Turner complained against South Florida Presbytery's action finding the Session of Cross Community Church guilty of important delinquencies related to alleged sexual abuse incidents involving the pastor's sons, without formal judicial process. The SJC denied the complaint as to Presbytery's right to investigate under BCO 40-4, but sustained it as to the finding of guilt and imposed censures, holding that formal judicial process (indictment, plea, and trial) under BCO 40-6 was required before findings of guilt could be entered, and remanded to Presbytery.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC ruled that Anna Lewis's BCO 40-5 report filed directly with the SJC was out of order, holding that the SJC's only responsibility under Chapter 40 arises upon referral from the General Assembly per RAO 16-10.c. Six members dissented, arguing the SJC has historically exercised direct jurisdiction over BCO 40-5 reports and that the majority's interpretation was overly narrow and a departure from settled precedent.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Tolivar Wills complained that Metro Atlanta Presbytery improperly dissolved Grace North Atlanta Church without following formal judicial process under BCO 40-6. The SJC denied the complaint, ruling that BCO 13-9(f) grants presbytery inherent authority to dissolve a church without mandating any specific procedure, and that the record did not demonstrate clear error in MAP's exercise of its discretion and judgment.

artifacts.title: Session of First Presbyterian Church North Port v. Presbytery of Southwest Florida
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained the Session of FPC North Port's complaint that Southwest Florida Presbytery erred when it remanded a previously out-of-order complaint back to the Session and when it directed and instructed the Session to initiate formal ecclesiastical process against a member without following the required steps of BCO 40-5. The Commission held that once the Original CM Complaint was found out of order, there was no matter for Presbytery to carry forward, and any subsequent instructions to the Session to initiate process were null and void.

artifacts.synopsis: Central Carolina Presbytery sent a memorial alleging that TE J. Steven Wilkins of Louisiana Presbytery was teaching doctrines (Federal Vision/Auburn Avenue theology) in flagrant contradiction to the Westminster Standards regarding election, covenant, and baptism. The SJC, after extended proceedings and directing Louisiana Presbytery to re-examine TE Wilkins, found Louisiana Presbytery had not adequately addressed the concerns and directed it via amends to appear under BCO 40-5 to account for its actions.
